title: Improve Blazor SSR client-side form validation
body:
## Summary Reworks the .NET Preview 5 client-side validation implementation for Blazor SSR forms. From a developer's point of view the feature is unchanged (add `` to a static SSR `EditForm` and validation runs in the browser), but the design underneath is substantially simpler and better layered: validation rules are delivered through a single inert per-form carrier element instead of `data-val-*` attributes on every input, all render-mode-specific code is out of the core `Forms` assembly, and the public surface shrinks to a small, purposeful set of types. Contributes to #51040. Addresses remaining feedback from https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/66420 and https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/66441. ## Background and motivation Preview 5 shipped an initial implementation that emitted MVC-style `data-val-*` attributes onto every input, generated by a public `IClientValidationService` living in the core `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms` assembly and read on the client by a DOM scanner. Follow-up architectural review raised three concerns this PR addresses: - Render-mode-specific logic (and the public client-validation service) lived in the core `Forms` assembly, where it does not belong. - The `data-val-*` approach spread validation metadata across many attributes on many elements and coupled the input components to the client-validation wire format. - The public API exposed the wire format (an attribute-dictionary service) as the extension point. ## What changed ### Wire format: one inert carrier element per form Instead of `data-val-*` attributes on each input, each static-SSR form emits a single custom element carrying all of the form's rules as JSON in a `data-rules` attribute: ```html ``` The JSON is encoder-escaped by the serializer and HTML-attribute-encoded by Blazor, so it is safe in the page and round-trips through `getAttribute` + `JSON.parse`. Because the payload is in an attribute (not element content), the element renders nothing and needs no CSS to stay hidden. However, the added element **can affect certain CSS selectors**. ### Assembly layering The feature is split across three assemblies along the existing `Endpoints` -> `Web` -> `Forms` reference direction: | Assembly | Responsibility | Visibility | |---|---|---| | `Forms` | The `EnableClientValidation` flag on `DataAnnotationsValidator`, and writing the activation signal into `EditContext.Properties`. No render logic. | public flag only | | `Web` | `EditForm`/`InputBase` integration: `InputBase` registers fields into an internal `RenderedFieldRegistry`, the internal `ClientValidationData` component emits the rule metadata, the `ClientValidationProvider` abstraction is the DI seam. | `ClientValidationProvider` public, rest internal | | `Endpoints` | The concrete `DataAnnotationsClientValidationProvider`, its cahces, and the JSON serialization. Maps DataAnnotations attributes to rules for server-validated fields only. | `ClientValidationRule` + `IClientValidationAdapter` public, rest internal | ### The provider returns a `RenderFragment` `ClientValidationProvider.RenderClientValidationRules(...)` returns a `RenderFragment?` that renders the carrier element (or `null` when there is nothing to emit). The `Web`-side `ClientValidationData` component simply renders that fragment; it never sees the descriptor types or the serializer, both of which are internal to `Endpoints`. This keeps the wire format fully owned by `Endpoints` and off the `Web` (and therefore WebAssembly) surface. ### Client ingestion: form-associated custom element `blazor.web.js` defines `` as a form-associated custom element. Its `connectedCallback` reads `data-rules`, finds the owning form via `attachInternals().form`, registers each field with the validation engine, and sets `novalidate` on the form; `disconnectedCallback` unregisters. The element also observes `data-rules`, so when an enhanced-navigation morph rewrites the payload of a reused carrier in place, `attributeChangedCallback` rebuilds that form's rules natively. This replaces the Preview 5 DOM scanner (`querySelectorAll('[data-val=true]')`), which is removed. ### Validation-state styling: Blazor's own classes, no configuration The JS engine applies the same CSS class names as Blazor's interactive validation: `invalid` / `valid` (with `modified` once the user edits a field) on inputs, `validation-message` on message elements, and `validation-summary-errors` / `validation-summary-valid` on the summary. A single stylesheet -- the default Blazor template CSS -- therefore styles static-SSR client-side validation and interactive validation identically, with no configuration. The Preview 5 `Blazor.start({ ssr: { formValidation: { cssClasses } } })` override is removed; there is no public JS configuration surface. This also fixes #67071 (valid-state styling differed across render modes): the engine now adds the `modified` class to a field once the user edits it, mirroring interactive `EditContext.IsModified`, so the template's `.valid.modified` green-outline rule applies in SSR exactly as it does interactively. ### `ValidationMessage` and `ValidationSummary` rendering Changes rendered HTML output of `ValidationMessage` and `ValidationSummary` so that: - **Interactive** render modes emit exactly the .NET 10 output. - **Static SSR** emits hidden placeholders (for the JS library to locate where to put messages from client-side validation) that otherwise have the same CSS-adding and attribute-splatting behaviors as the interactive paths. ### JS validators aligned with .NET attributes The Phone and the Credit card JS validators had stricter rules than their .NET attribute counterparts. The JS validators are now intentionally simplified to accept the same inputs. Users are free to implement stricter validation rules as needed. ### Client-side validation runs only when server-side would The Preview 5 implementation emits and runs client-side validation rules even when the respective validation attributes are not validated by the server-side validation (e.g., for nested properties when `AddValidation` has not been enabled). This PR changes this behavior so that client-side rules are not emitted in such cases. The reason is that we don't want fields that would not get validation on the server (which is authoritative) to be validated on the client (which is a UX improvement) to not give developers a false sense of security. A developer could think the data they are getting from the form is properly validated - meanwhile, the client-side validation can be sidestepped by disabling/modifying the JS code. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Server["Server (static SSR)"] DAV["DataAnnotationsValidator
writes activation flag
keyed by its own type"] IB["InputBase
registers rendered field + name
(AssignedRenderMode is null)"] CVD["ClientValidationData (internal)
checks activation + provider,
renders provider fragment"] Prov["DataAnnotationsClientValidationProvider
DataAnnotations to rules -> JSON
(only server-validated fields)"] DAV --> IB --> CVD Prov --> CVD end subgraph HTML["Rendered HTML"] Carrier["blazor-client-validation-data
data-rules='{...}'"] end subgraph Client["blazor.web.js"] FACE["Form-associated custom element
connectedCallback + attributeChangedCallback"] Engine["ValidationEngine + validators
ErrorDisplay + EventManager"] FACE --> Engine end CVD --> Carrier Carrier --> FACE Engine -->|"blocks invalid submit,
shows messages"| HTML ``` 1. `DataAnnotationsValidator` writes the activation flag into `EditContext.Properties[typeof(DataAnnotationsValidator)]` when `EnableClientValidation` is `true` (the default). 2. During static SSR only (`AssignedRenderMode is null`), each `InputBase` registers its `FieldIdentifier` and rendered HTML `name` into a per-form `RenderedFieldRegistry`. 3. `ClientValidationData` (rendered by `EditForm` after its `ChildContent`, so it initializes after the inputs register) checks the activation flag, resolves the optional `ClientValidationProvider`, reads the registry, and renders the provider's fragment. 4. `DataAnnotationsClientValidationProvider` builds rules from the model's DataAnnotations attributes and returns a fragment that emits the carrier, emitting client rules only for fields the server would also validate (see Security below). 5. On the client, the custom element registers the form's fields, suppresses native browser validation, and validates on interaction. Invalid submissions are blocked in the capture phase (including enhanced-navigation submits). ## Public API Public surface after this PR: ```csharp // Assembly: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms; public class DataAnnotationsValidator // existing type { // Opt a form in/out of client-side validation. Default true. public bool EnableClientValidation { get; set; } } ``` ```csharp // Assembly: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms.ClientValidation; // The DI seam. A host returns a RenderFragment that renders the carrier for the rendered fields, // or null when there is nothing to emit. Implemented internally by Components.Endpoints. public abstract class ClientValidationProvider { public abstract RenderFragment? RenderClientValidationRules( EditContext editContext, IReadOnlyDictionary renderedFields); } ``` ```csharp // Assembly: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Endpoints namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms; // A single client-side validation rule contributed by an IClientValidationAdapter. Rule names match // a validator registered on the JS side. The framework attaches each rule's resolved (and, when a // localizer is configured, localized) error message, so adapters supply only the rule shape. public sealed class ClientValidationRule { public ClientValidationRule(string name, IReadOnlyDictionary? parameters = null); public string Name { get; } public IReadOnlyDictionary? Parameters { get; } // string values on the wire } // Opt a custom ValidationAttribute into emitting client-side rules. public interface IClientValidationAdapter { IEnumerable GetClientValidationRules(); } ``` Everything else is internal: `ClientValidationData` and `RenderedFieldRegistry` (Web); `DataAnnotationsClientValidationProvider`, `ClientValidationCache`, and `ClientValidationDataWriter` (Endpoints). Removed from Preview 5 (superseded): `IClientValidationService`, the `AddClientValidation` DI extension, and the old `object?`-parameter `ClientValidationRule` (with `WithParameter`). The Preview 5 types lived in `Forms`; the reworked feature exposes no client-validation types from `Forms` at all. ## Behavior - **Zero-config activation.** No change for developers: adding `` to a static-SSR `EditForm` activates client validation. `EnableClientValidation="false"` opts out. - **Enhanced navigation is fully supported.** Enhanced nav patches the page by DOM morphing, which reuses the carrier element in place (so its `connectedCallback` does not re-fire) and strips the JS-added `novalidate`. Two mechanisms cover this: when the morph rewrites a reused carrier's `data-rules`, the element's `attributeChangedCallback` rebuilds that form's rules natively; and because the morph strips `novalidate` even when the rules are unchanged (so no attribute change fires), `ensureNovalidateOnForms()` runs on `enhancedload` to re-assert it. Covered by E2E for the form-to-form round-trip, form-to-no-form, and no-form-to-form transitions. - **Streaming-added inputs are a documented limitation.** Inputs added to an already-rendered form by a later streamed batch are not covered by client validation (they still validate on the server). A whole form delivered in a single streamed batch is covered. - **Security: rules are only emitted for server-validated fields.** The provider gates each field on whether the server would validate it on submit (based on whether the MEV path with nested validation support is used), so client validation never gives a false sense of coverage for fields the server ignores. - **XSS-safe payload.** The serializer uses `Utf8JsonWriter` (default encoder escapes `<`, `>`, `&`, `'`) combined with Blazor's HTML attribute encoding, so a hostile validation message cannot break out of the carrier element or its attribute. - **Consistent styling across render modes, no configuration.** The engine emits Blazor's own validation CSS classes (`invalid`/`valid`/`modified`, `validation-message`, `validation-summary-*`), so the default template stylesheet styles static-SSR and interactive validation identically. Fixes #67071.
